PROJECT PROPOSAL – 972 Lewis St., Memphis, TN 38107
Project Overview
This proposal covers a substantial renovation of 972 Lewis St., Memphis, TN 38107, an approximately 960 sq. ft., 2-bedroom / 1-bath property. The renovation includes roofing, windows, exterior repairs and painting, driveway improvements, tree and landscaping work, HVAC replacement, interior reconfiguration, new flooring, drywall and framing repairs, a new kitchen, full bathroom renovation, plumbing and electrical improvements, insulation, doors, hardware, and final property cleanup.

Project Solution
Delta Ridge Renovations will renovate and reconfigure the property to improve functionality, appearance, and long-term rental performance. The planned layout modifications include removing one exterior door and window, opening the kitchen into the living area, incorporating a laundry area, modifying a closet and bathroom area, and utilizing available space to create an additional bedroom.

The completed renovation will include a new kitchen with appliances, a fully renovated bathroom, new flooring, updated electrical and plumbing systems, HVAC replacement with required ductwork, interior and exterior finishes, and associated structural and finish repairs. Final colors and finishes will follow Delta Ridge Renovations' design standards, with a detailed design layout provided upon project approval.

1. Window Replacement
Replacing old windows improves energy efficiency, insulation, appearance, and security.

Work Included
Removal of existing windows and old framing materials
Inspection for water damage, mold, or wood rot around openings
Installation of new energy-efficient windows (double-pane or insulated glass)
Sealing and flashing around frames to prevent leaks
Interior and exterior trim replacement as needed
Caulking and insulation around window openings
Common Upgrades
Vinyl or aluminum-clad windows
Low-E glass for energy savings
Tempered glass where required by code
Black or modern-style frames for updated curb appeal
Benefits
Lower utility bills
Reduced drafts and outside noise
Improved property value
Updated exterior appearance

2. Drywall Replacement and Repair
Drywall work restores damaged walls and ceilings while preparing the interior for a modern finish.

Work Included
Demolition and removal of damaged drywall
Replacement of water-damaged or cracked wall sections
Installation of new drywall panels
Taping, mudding, sanding, and finishing joints
Ceiling repairs and texture matching
Corner bead replacement and wall straightening
Areas Commonly Repaired
Bathrooms and kitchens with moisture damage
Areas opened for plumbing/electrical upgrades
Cracked seams from settling
Damaged tenant areas
Finish Preparation
Primer application
Surface smoothing for paint-ready walls
Texture application if desired (smooth, orange peel, knockdown)

3. Plumbing Updates
Updating plumbing ensures safety, reliability, and code compliance while reducing future maintenance issues.

Work Included
Replacement of outdated galvanized or polybutylene piping
Installation of new PEX or copper water supply lines
Drain and sewer line inspection or replacement
New shut-off valves and water connections
Replacement of plumbing fixtures and fittings
Water heater upgrades if needed
Typical Duplex Plumbing Improvements
Separate shut-offs for each unit
Bathroom and kitchen plumbing modernization
Leak repairs and pressure balancing
Updated venting systems
Washer/dryer hookup improvements
Benefits
Improved water pressure
Reduced risk of leaks and water damage
Better efficiency and reliability
Easier future maintenance

4. Electrical System Upgrades
Electrical upgrades modernize the duplex for safety and increased power demand.

Work Included
Removal of outdated wiring (cloth wiring, aluminum wiring, knob-and-tube if present)
Installation of new copper wiring
Upgrading electrical panels and breakers
Adding grounded outlets throughout units
GFCI and AFCI protection installation
New switches, receptacles, and lighting fixtures
Additional Upgrades
Dedicated appliance circuits
Smoke and carbon monoxide detector installation
Exterior security lighting
Ceiling fan wiring
USB outlets or smart-home features
Safety Improvements
Code-compliant grounding
Proper load balancing
Surge protection options
Updated service capacity (100–200 amp service)

5. Exterior Repainting
Exterior painting protects the duplex from weather while dramatically improving curb appeal.

Preparation Work
Pressure washing exterior surfaces
Scraping loose or peeling paint
Sanding rough areas
Repairing wood trim and siding damage
Caulking gaps and seams
Priming bare surfaces
Painting Process
Application of weather-resistant exterior paint
Painting siding, trim, soffits, fascia, and doors
Optional repainting of shutters, railings, or porches
Spray, brush, or roller application depending on surfaces
Common Paint Choices
Acrylic exterior paint
UV-resistant finishes
Neutral modern color palettes
Satin or semi-gloss trim finishes

Benefits
Improved weather protection
Increased property value
Better tenant appeal
Extended life of siding and trim

**Permit Project Description**  
**Owner:** Patricia Duncan Harrison  
**Property:** 4479 Julia Cove, Millington, TN 38053  
**Contractor:** Homeway Construction & Restoration

Interior residential renovation to improve accessibility, remodel the primary bathroom, and construct a new half bathroom within the existing garage area. Work includes:

- **Primary bathroom:** Remove the existing bathtub and install an accessible roll-in shower with handheld shower wand, single-lever controls, grab bars, and shower enclosure with a 36-inch clear opening. Modify the existing partition wall and install an accessible sink with protected piping and an accessible toilet with grab bars. Convert the existing shower and linen closet into a larger linen closet. Install tile flooring and a new exhaust fan. Widen the bathroom doorway and install a 36-inch sliding door.
- **New garage half bathroom:** Frame and finish a half bathroom with an accessible toilet, sink, grab bars, tile flooring, and a 36-inch swing-out door connecting to the kitchen. Install required plumbing, electrical, and ventilation. Saw-cut and remove portions of the concrete slab in the garage and along the hallway to install a new drain line connecting to the existing main sewer inside the house. Restore the slab and affected finishes after rough-in inspections.
- **Flooring:** Remove and replace existing carpet and tile throughout the house, excluding the existing hallway bathroom. Replace carpeted areas with hardwood flooring and replace tiled areas with new tile. Install transitions, trim, and shoe molding as required.
- **Doorways and accessibility:** Widen the sleeping-room hallway doorway to 36 inches. Remove the existing 32-inch rear exterior door and widen the opening for a 36-inch door, including required framing and brick modifications. Install a transition ramp at the designated living-room doorway.
- **Additional work:** Replace the existing smaller water heater with a 50-gallon unit. Complete associated drywall repairs, painting, and finish restoration.

The existing hallway bathroom is excluded from the renovation. All work will be performed in accordance with applicable building codes and required inspections.

Residential exterior renovation consisting of demolition and removal of two existing rear deck structures and construction of a new approximately 18' × 17' elevated pressure-treated wood deck with new footings, structural framing, support posts/columns, stairs, handrails/guardrails, and decking. The deck framing will incorporate structural support for a new covered porch roof.

Construct an approximately 18' × 16' covered, screened-in porch over the new deck, including a new gable-style roof tied into the existing residence, structural headers, beams, rafters, ceiling framing, roof decking, underlayment, flashing, architectural shingles, screened wall framing, approximately 3' knee walls, Hardie siding, exterior trim, screening, and screen door installation.

Additional work includes construction of an approximately 10' × 32' exterior concrete patio, including excavation, compacted base, reinforcement, approximately 4"" concrete slab, drainage slope, control joints, and exposed-aggregate finish.

Associated improvements include electrical work for the covered porch, including ceiling fan wiring, switches and GFCI-protected exterior receptacles; relocation of the existing dryer exhaust vent; installation of gutters and downspouts; approximately 360 SF of beadboard gable ceiling; and exterior painting/finishing of the new construction.

All construction to comply with applicable building and electrical codes and approved permit requirements. Final structural framing, footing sizes, roof connections, and attachment methods are subject to field verification and applicable code/plan-review requirements.

Original Duplex House was converted into an office space for Oasis of Hope.   We are turning the property into a single family home.   Converting one office back to the original Kitchen. Adding back a Laundry Room.   Demolishing some interior walls and reframing for a new layout.

The project includes construction of a 7,100-square-foot rubberized splash pad area featuring 76 spray elements. The site will also include a 40-foot-diameter fabric shade structure with five picnic tables beneath it.

Additional project components include installation of a 13’ x 31’ prefabricated equipment storage building, as well as site amenities adjacent to the splash pad such as benches, trash receptacles, bicycle racks, a drinking fountain, and two-rail wood fencing.

To improve site access, 32 new parking spaces will be added along the entrance road from Park Avenue, expanding the current 80 spaces to a total of 112.

All overhead electrical wires will be relocated underground and utility poles removed.  MLGW lease lighting will provide additional light poles along the parking/drive.  Contractor will be required to coordinate this work with MLGW.

The City of Memphis will provide the following materials for contractor installation: Vortex spray equipment, USA Shade structure, Poligon building, and Dumor site fixtures.
